question: Name the Indian sitar player who became a hippie music icon of the 1960s after collaborating with the Beatles.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Pt. Ravi Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pt. Ravi Shankar** was a legendary Indian sitar player and composer, often referred to as the **Godfather of World Music**.
 
• He gained international fame during the **1960s** after collaborating with **The Beatles**, especially with **George Harrison**.
 
• His music became emblematic of the **hippie movement** and was instrumental in introducing Indian classical music to the Western audience.
 
• He performed at iconic events such as the **Monterey Pop Festival** (1967) and **Woodstock** (1969).
 
• Pt. Ravi Shankar was also a major contributor to the development of the sitar as a global instrument and worked with various artists, including **Philip Glass** and **Yehudi Menuhin**.
 
• He received numerous accolades, including **Bharat Ratna** (India’s highest civilian award) and several **Grammy Awards**.
 
• His work laid the foundation for the fusion of **Indian and Western music styles**, influencing genres such as jazz, rock, and world music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt**__

 __
 
• **Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt** is an Indian slide guitarist and the creator of the **Mohan Veena**, a modified slide guitar.
 
• He is a Grammy Award winner for his album **"A Meeting by the River"** with Ry Cooder.
 
• His focus has been on blending Indian classical music with other global styles.
 
 
 
• **Pt. Shiv Kumar Sharma**__
 __
 
• **Pt. Shiv Kumar Sharma** was a renowned **santoor** maestro who popularized the instrument in Indian classical music.
 
• He collaborated with **Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia** to compose music for Hindi films, including the iconic film **"Silsila."**
 
 
 
• **Pt. Ram Narayan**__
 
 
• **Pt. Ram Narayan** was a celebrated **sarangi player** known for his expressive renditions of Indian classical music.
 
• He was instrumental in elevating the sarod as a solo instrument on the global stage.
